question: An agent that calls your internal tools occasionally runs for minutes, repeats the same write twice and then times out. Which change addresses the root cause?
context: The loop is: ask the model what to do, call the tool it names, feed the result back, repeat until it says it is done. Tools include "create refund" and "send email".

options.label: Give it a step budget, idempotent tools and a deadline per call
options.why: The loop has no bound, so it can spin; the tools are not safe to repeat, so a retried step duplicates work. Bounding the loop, making each tool idempotent and putting a deadline on each call fixes all three symptoms at their source.

options.label: Prompt it more firmly to stop when finished
options.why: Instructions in a prompt are a request, not a guarantee. Control that must hold belongs in the code around the model, not in the text you send it.

options.label: Cache the model responses so repeats are cheaper
options.why: Cheaper repeats are still repeats: the refund is still created twice. Caching hides the cost of the bug rather than removing it.

options.label: Replace the loop with a scripted pipeline
options.why: Often the right call, and worth considering — a fixed sequence is easier to test and cheaper to run. But it is a redesign, not a fix for the loop you have in production today.
